absent: Exact bit positions and widths of locked, pending, tail, and slow fields outside the stated masks and values.
Spin threshold values and underlying halt, wake, and kick mechanics of the paravirtual primitives.
Full queue-node MCS grant handshake and unlock-contended handoff beyond the cited fragments.
Complete RT mutex common blocking, chain-walk, takeover, and waiter-fixup algorithms beyond the shown call sites.
Remaining lock-event identifiers, file wiring, and threshold tuning for statistics interfaces.

findings.text: Visible paravirtual unlock operation attempts a fast release of the locked byte and otherwise delegates to a slow routine that resolves a hashed waiter before releasing.
Early initialization operation sizes and allocates the global paravirtual lock hash table used to find halted waiters at unlock time.
Statistics read operation aggregates one per-CPU lock-event counter across possible CPUs and formats either a raw total, a per-kick average latency, or a hops-per-kick decimal value.
Public RT mutex blocking operations cover uninterruptible nested acquisition with subclass, acquisition with an explicit nesting lock, interruptible acquisition, and killable acquisition.

Public RT mutex helpers initialize a mutex base object, attempt nonblocking acquisition with lock dependency tracking, adjust priority inheritance for a task, and validate that an exiting task has no priority-inheritance state.
Boot option handler records a request to disable paravirtual spinning; sysctl initializer publishes the maximum RT lock depth; hash initializer runs early to allocate the waiter lookup table.
Queue node embeds an MCS node and, under paravirtual spinning, reservation space sized to hold paravirtual per-node data.
Paravirtual node extends an MCS node with an owning CPU identifier and a small virtual-CPU state field; hash entry pairs a contended lock address with its blocked node pointer.
Virtual-CPU waiter state has three values denoting running, halted while waiting in queue, and halted plus present in the lock hash table.
Queue depth limit constant equals four.
Pending spin loop count constant equals one.
Slow-path locked marker has numeric value three positioned at the locked field offset.
Predecessor state sampling mask equals 255, so only one iteration in 256 performs the predecessor check.
Combined locked-or-pending mask is the union of the locked mask and the pending mask.
Hash geometry derives entries per cache line from cache bytes per entry size and minimum table size from page size per entry size.
Default maximum RT lock depth equals 1024 and is exposed as a writable kernel sysctl named max_lock_depth.
Tail exchange preserves the existing locked and pending portion while installing a caller-supplied tail, looping on relaxed compare-exchange and returning the prior word.
Pending acquisition uses an acquire fetch-or of the pending value; locked marking is a single unsynchronized store of the locked value.

Pending handling has two shapes: a byte-oriented form that stores pending and acquires by clearing pending while setting locked only when unlocked, and a word-oriented form that ORs pending and then clears pending while setting locked unless locked is observed.

Paravirtual trylock is aliased to a hybrid unfair attempt that steals a free unpended lock with an acquire compare-exchange, keeps spinning while queue tail exists without pending, and otherwise gives up.
Hash table iteration starts at the cache-line-aligned bucket for the hashed address and linearly wraps across a power-of-two number of buckets.
Hop accounting either adds the probe count to a per-CPU counter selected by event name or compiles to nothing, depending on build configuration.
Wait and kick shims forward to underlying primitives; instrumented wrappers additionally record kick issue time per CPU and accumulate kick and wake latencies around the wait.
Node initialization records the current CPU and marks the waiter running, after a compile-time check that paravirtual node fits in the generic queue node reservation.
Predecessor early-exit check samples the previous waiter state only on masked iterations and reports non-running as a reason to stop spinning early.
Hash insertion probes for a vacant slot, claims it atomically, publishes the waiter node, reports probe length, and treats absence of any free slot as impossible.
Hash removal scans for the entry matching the unlocking address, publishes the stored node to the caller, clears the slot, and treats a missing entry as impossible.
Hash table allocation requests four entries per possible CPU rounded up to cache-line granularity and at least one page worth of entries, zeroed from early boot memory.

Queue waiter publication relies on ordered store of halted state before rechecking the grant flag, paired with a kick-side barrier plus state compare-exchange and release/acquire handling of the grant flag.
Head waiter must publish its hash entry before publishing the slow value, paired with a read barrier after observing the slow value at unlock so the hash entry is visible to the unlocker.

Queue waiter first spins for grant or early predecessor halt, then publishes halted and sleeps unless already granted, then restores running unless already hashed by the kicker, and repeats after spurious wakeups while retaining hashed state.
Kicker advances a halted waiter to hashed and only then marks the lock slow and inserts the hash entry; failure to advance means the waiter stayed running and will observe the grant itself.

Head waiter marks itself running, enables pending, spins for lock acquisition, hashes exactly once, exchanges slow into the lock with immediate reclaim if the lock was free, otherwise marks itself hashed and sleeps on the slow value until acquisition.

Unlock takes a fast release when the lock holds plain locked; otherwise it validates the slow marker, orders hash lookup after that observation, unhashes, releases with release semantics, then kicks the recorded CPU.
RT waiter order is primarily priority order, with wound-wait stamp order breaking priority ties when both waiters carry contexts; priority-inheritance waiter order uses priority order alone.
RT fast acquisition first attempts an acquire compare-exchange from unowned to current and falls back to a slow try operation on failure.
RT lock try operation rejects non-task context under debugging, performs the fast-or-slow attempt, and records lock dependency acquisition on success.

RT slow lock runs under the waiter lock with interrupts disabled, attempts immediate takeover, enqueues the current task in a dedicated wait state, then alternates takeover attempts with owner spinning or sleeping while dropping and reacquiring the waiter lock, finally restoring task state and repairing waiter flags.
Uninterruptible RT lock wrappers treat any return from the common blocking path as unreachable and warn, since that path only returns on signal or timeout which those callers do not use.

Priority adjustment rewalks the blocking chain only when the task remains blocked and its effective priority differs from its waiter node; task teardown warns if priority waiters or a blocked-on pointer remain.

Exhausted hash table during insertion, missing hash entry during removal, and an unlock slow path observing a value other than slow are treated as fatal or corruption-warning conditions rather than normal races.
Statistics read rejects an out-of-range counter identifier; RT trylock from invalid context warns and fails instead of acquiring.
